title: Continuous integration that blocks unapproved public APIs
hook: Every public type in a shared library is a contract. Continuous integration (CI) can diff public API surface between builds and fail pull requests that add breaking changes without approval — the same discipline product teams use before publishing NuGet packages.

blocks.text: Public API analyzers compare the exported surface of an assembly between a baseline and the current build. Adding a method might be compatible; removing or changing signature is breaking. Tools like Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.PublicApiAnalyzers, ApiCompat, or custom scripts on reflection output gate merges. Pair with semantic versioning and InternalsVisibleTo so experiments stay internal until ready.

entries.plainDefinition: All public and protected types and members visible to consumers of an assembly.
entries.example: public class OrderService { public Task Submit() }

entries.plainDefinition: Tooling that compares two builds for API compatibility.
entries.example: CI fails if a public method is removed.

entries.plainDefinition: Change that forces consumers to recompile or breaks at runtime.
entries.example: Renaming a public method or changing parameter types.

blocks.text: A domain package referenced by three microservices cannot casually rename public DTOs. CI guards catch accidental public exposure of internal types. Interviewers ask how you prevent library semver violations — answer with access modifiers, review radar, and automated API diff in pull request checks.

blocks.title: Default to internal
blocks.body: Make new types internal until you deliberately expose them. Public is a publishing decision.

diagram.title: CI public API check
diagram.source:
flowchart TD
  A[Pull request build] --> B[Compile library]
  B --> C[Extract public API]
  C --> D{Diff vs baseline}
  D -->|Compatible| E[Merge allowed]
  D -->|Breaking| F[Fail CI require review]

snippet.label: PublicApiAnalyzers package
snippet.explanation: Adds RS0016 and related diagnostics when public API changes without updating Shipped/Unshipped txt files.

snippet.label: Keep experiments internal
snippet.explanation: Internal engine can change freely. Public facade is the stable contract CI watches.

snippet.label: CI api compat check
snippet.code:
dotnet build -c Release
# ApiCompat or custom tool:
dotnet-apicompat --baseline artifacts/MyLib.1.0.0.dll --current bin/Release/net10.0/MyLib.dll
snippet.explanation: Pipeline step blocks merge when binary compatibility breaks without approval.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Making everything public for convenience. Forgetting to update PublicAPI files so CI always fails. Changing public record positional parameter order — breaking for callers.

interviewTakeaways: Public API is a published contract — guard it in CI.
Default new code to internal; expose deliberately.
ApiCompat and PublicApiAnalyzers catch accidental breaks.
commonPitfalls: Public types that should be internal.
Breaking record or interface changes without major version bump.
